entries.name: GOV.UK Design System
entries.scope: Initial viewport at 390x900 and 1440x900, reduced motion, cookie notice visible. No interactions exercised.
entries.typography: Computed h1: GDS Transport, arial, sans-serif; 32px/35px at 390, 48px/50px at 1440.
entries.layout: Desktop navigation and search share a wide container; mobile stacks search and Menu. Cookie notice occupies a substantial first-screen area.
entries.color: Rendered blue hero, white type and green cookie actions; computed body background white. No contrast audit performed.
entries.motion: Not tested; capture used reduced-motion preference.
observations: Clear hierarchy connects the service-design task to a direct start action.
Desktop illustration supports the explanation while mobile prioritizes text.
No document overflow measured at either sampled width.
strengths: Legible type and predictable content grouping
weaknesses: Cookie notice delays first-screen access to the main action; a contextual tradeoff, not proof of poor UX.
entries.use_when: Service interfaces and information-heavy systems need recognizable task structure.
entries.implementation: Separate navigation, search and content landmarks; use semantic components and a mobile reading order based on task priority.
limitations: No full accessibility audit, keyboard test or performance measurement.
Font family is a computed declaration, not a redistribution license.

entries.name: Linear
entries.scope: Text and computed h1 styles inspected at 390 and 1440. Browser screenshots showed navigation but blank hero even after a load/heading readiness retry; visual analysis is incomplete.
entries.typography: Computed h1 declares Inter Variable; 38px/41.8px at 390, 64px/64px at 1440. Screenshot did not expose the heading.
entries.layout: Only navigation was visibly confirmed; remaining composition cannot be inferred from DOM text.
entries.color: Computed body rgb(8,9,10), h1 rgb(247,248,248); no contrast audit.
entries.motion: Unknown; reduced-motion capture did not show hero. No cause established.
observations: Text content includes detailed product issue and review context rather than only abstract marketing.
No document overflow measured at sampled widths; that does not establish visual completeness.
strengths: Product-specific content provides a useful communication pattern.
weaknesses: Visual review limited by incomplete rendering in this environment; not a finding against the live product.
entries.use_when: Explain a software workflow with concrete task content.
entries.implementation: Build an original preview showing your own product's meaningful state and action; do not copy Linear's identity.
limitations: No complete rendered hero, interaction, accessibility or performance evaluation.

entries.name: Figma
entries.scope: Text and DOM computed values inspected at 390 and 1440. Screenshots remained blank after load/heading readiness retry; expressive classification is a research candidate, not a rendered finding.
entries.typography: Computed h1 declares figmaSans with fallbacks; 36px/36px mobile and 56px/56px desktop.
entries.layout: Text exposes a product-family navigation hierarchy. No visual composition verified.
entries.color: Computed h1 black, body transparent; actual composite background not inferred.
observations: Product families are described by user activity in the textual navigation.
DOM overflow flag was true at both sampled widths; with blank screenshots the cause and user impact are unresolved.
strengths: Action-based product grouping is a useful information-architecture pattern.
weaknesses: Cannot assess visual quality from the available captures.
entries.use_when: A suite needs understandable grouping by task.
entries.implementation: Name product groups around user goals and keep navigation semantics independent of art direction.
limitations: No verified visual style, interaction, accessibility or performance result.

entries.name: Stripe
entries.scope: Live page textual content only; web retrieval redirected to /en-ch.
entries.layout: Text distinguishes payments, billing and other product groups; rendered composition not inspected.
observations: Text includes billing usage and transaction-related context alongside product categories.
Self-serve and sales-contact actions address different visitor needs.
strengths: Product examples connect broad infrastructure claims to specific use cases.
weaknesses: Large product scope may increase navigation cost; this is a hypothesis requiring task testing.
entries.use_when: A complex offering needs concrete examples and audience-specific entry points.
entries.implementation: Use factual task examples, meaningful units and clearly distinguished next actions.
limitations: No rendered typography, responsive behavior, interaction or performance claims.

entries.name: Lusion v3 — award research lead
entries.scope: Awwwards archive entry only; live site not inspected.
observations: Lusion v3 appears in the Awwwards Sites of the Year archive with a 2023 label.
strengths: A primary award archive provides a traceable lead for historical study.
weaknesses: Archive text alone cannot reveal why the design works.
entries.use_when: Selecting a historical creative-site case for deeper inspection.
entries.implementation: Inspect the awarded version and current site separately before borrowing any design principle.

awards.designation: Listed in Sites of the Year archive

limitations: Not asserted to be the single jury grand-prize winner.
No live-site analysis; do not use as validated design guidance.
